nodes.summary: If `A` and `B` commute then `tr e^{A + B} ≤ tr (e^A e^B)` in the partial order of `ℂ`, with equality. This is only the restriction to commuting matrices of the Golden–Thompson inequality (Forrester and Thompson, arXiv:1408.2008v1, equation (1.1)); the general case is wanted.
nodes.title: Golden–Thompson inequality for commuting matrices

nodes.summary: For Hermitian complex matrices `A` and `B`, `tr e^{A + B} ≤ tr (e^A e^B)` (P. J. Forrester and C. J. Thompson, *The Golden–Thompson inequality — historical aspects and random matrix applications*, arXiv:1408.2008v1, equation (1.1); S. Golden, Phys. Rev. 137 (1965) B1127; C. J. Thompson, J. Math. Phys. 6 (1965) 1812). The inequality is taken in the partial order of `ℂ`, so it also asserts that the right side is…
nodes.title: Golden–Thompson inequality

nodes.summary: If `A` and `B` commute then `tr e^{A + B} = tr (e^A e^B)`, because `e^{A + B} = e^A e^B` (`Matrix.exp_add_of_commute`). This is the equality case of the Golden–Thompson inequality (Forrester and Thompson, arXiv:1408.2008v1, equation (1.1)); no Hermitian hypothesis is needed.
nodes.title: Golden–Thompson equality for commuting matrices

nodes.summary: For Hermitian `A` and `B`, `0 ≤ tr (e^A e^B)` in the partial order of `ℂ`, that is, the trace is real and nonnegative. Indeed `tr (e^A e^B) = tr (X Xᴴ)` with `X = e^{A/2} e^{B/2}`. So the Golden–Thompson inequality `tr e^{A + B} ≤ tr (e^A e^B)` (Forrester and Thompson, arXiv:1408.2008v1, equation (1.1)) compares two real numbers even though `e^A e^B` need not be Hermitian.
nodes.title: The right side of Golden–Thompson is a nonnegative real
